data.title: Afcons Infrastructure Limited Just Missed Earnings - But Analysts Have Updated Their Models
data.description:
Afcons Infrastructure Limited (NSE:AFCONS) missed earnings with its latest second-quarter results, disappointing overly-optimistic forecasters. Results showed a clear earnings miss, with ₹26b revenue coming in 3.8% lower than what the analystsexpected. Statutory earnings per share (EPS) of ₹1.12 missed the mark badly, arriving some 38% below what was expected. Earnings are an important time for investors, as they can track a company's performance, look at what the analysts are forecasting for next year, and see if there's been a change in sentiment towards the company. Readers will be glad to know we've aggregated the latest statutory forecasts to see whether the analysts have changed their mind on Afcons Infrastructure after the latest results.

We've found 21 US stocks that are forecast to pay a dividend yield of over 6% next year. See the full list for free.

Taking into account the latest results, the consensus forecast from Afcons Infrastructure's ten analysts is for revenues of ₹122.7b in 2027. This reflects a solid 11% improvement in revenue compared to the last 12 months. Per-share earnings are expected to leap 299% to ₹8.73. Before this earnings report, the analysts had been forecasting revenues of ₹122.7b and earnings per share (EPS) of ₹8.78 in 2027. The consensus analysts don't seem to have seen anything in these results that would have changed their view on the business, given there's been no major change to their estimates.

Check out our latest analysis for Afcons Infrastructure

With no major changes to earnings forecasts, the consensus price target fell 11% to ₹318, suggesting that the analysts might have previously been hoping for an earnings upgrade. It could also be instructive to look at the range of analyst estimates, to evaluate how different the outlier opinions are from the mean. The most optimistic Afcons Infrastructure analyst has a price target of ₹377 per share, while the most pessimistic values it at ₹202. This shows there is still a bit of diversity in estimates, but analysts don't appear to be totally split on the stock as though it might be a success or failure situation.

Taking a look at the bigger picture now, one of the ways we can understand these forecasts is to see how they compare to both past performance and industry growth estimates. One thing stands out from these estimates, which is that Afcons Infrastructure is forecast to grow faster in the future than it has in the past, with revenues expected to display 23% annualised growth until the end of 2027. If achieved, this would be a much better result than the 14% annual decline over the past year. By contrast, our data suggests that other companies (with analyst coverage) in the industry are forecast to see their revenue grow 13% per year. So it looks like Afcons Infrastructure is expected to grow faster than its competitors, at least for a while.

The Bottom Line

The most important thing to take away is that there's been no major change in sentiment, with the analysts reconfirming that the business is performing in line with their previous earnings per share estimates. Fortunately, they also reconfirmed their revenue numbers, suggesting that it's tracking in line with expectations. Additionally, our data suggests that revenue is expected to grow faster than the wider industry. Furthermore, the analysts also cut their price targets, suggesting that the latest news has led to greater pessimism about the intrinsic value of the business.

Keeping that in mind, we still think that the longer term trajectory of the business is much more important for investors to consider. We have estimates - from multiple Afcons Infrastructure analysts - going out to 2029, and you can see them free on our platform here.

data.title: What Greggs Doubters Overlooked
data.description:
Greggs has not just been opening more shops and consulting on factory closures. It has been reshaping how and where it serves food on the go. Holding Greggs over the past year would have returned 56.9%, including dividends. If you had put money to work before that run, you would have been weighing bullish expansion plans against worries about UK quick-service saturation. What exactly did buyers think they were seeing that justified that call?

Greggs has already moved. See which of 15 high quality undervalued stocks still trade below our estimates.

The Two Greggs Stories Investors Had To Price In

The shares cost £15.76 at the start of the period, and anyone looking at Greggs then had to choose which story felt more convincing.

The bullish narrative pointed to a Fair Value of £20.66, a notional price level implied if expansion and digital ordering played out as hoped. That view leaned on Greggs growing revenue through more drive-thrus, retail parks and digital channels, supported by supply chain investments and a focus on value.

The cautious camp worked off a Fair Value of £13.3, a hypothetical price if risks dominated. This side focused on UK quick-service saturation, stricter regulation and rising costs, which could pressure profit margins and limit the benefit of new locations.

What The Results Changed For The Greggs Debate

The most concrete update came from Greggs reporting H1 2026 revenue of £1,101.5m and net income of £56.2m, with net margin at 5.1% versus 4.5% a year earlier. That backed the optimistic case that supply chain spending and new channels could support both sales and profitability. Factory closure plans and 740 proposed redundancies cut the other way, so the evidence still landed mixed.

The practical takeaway is simple. When a thesis leans on efficiency and format expansion, track margin percentage and shop count in each set of results to see if that story is actually turning into cash profit.

What Greggs' Run Up To £23.4 Already Assumes

Greggs now trades at £23.4, and the selected Narrative’s Fair Value sits below that level. The argument is not that the business is broken. It is that the current tag already bakes in clean supply chain execution and strong cash generation translating into generous capital returns.

Anyone paying today is effectively assuming multichannel growth, logistics projects and factory closures slot into place without hurting service or long term earnings. The question is how that assumption holds up if the supply chain programme or future cash return decisions play out differently from what buyers are now implying.

data.title: Nila Spaces (NSE:NILASPACES) Posted Healthy Earnings But There Are Some Other Factors To Be Aware Of
data.description:
Last week's profit announcement from Nila Spaces Limited (NSE:NILASPACES) was underwhelming for investors, despite headline numbers being robust. Our analysis uncovered some concerning factors that we believe the market might be paying attention to.

Trump has pledged to "unleash" American oil and gas and these 15 US stocks have developments that are poised to benefit.

A Closer Look At Nila Spaces' Earnings

As finance nerds would already know, the accrual ratio from cashflow is a key measure for assessing how well a company's free cash flow (FCF) matches its profit. To get the accrual ratio we first subtract FCF from profit for a period, and then divide that number by the average operating assets for the period. This ratio tells us how much of a company's profit is not backed by free cashflow.

As a result, a negative accrual ratio is a positive for the company, and a positive accrual ratio is a negative. That is not intended to imply we should worry about a positive accrual ratio, but it's worth noting where the accrual ratio is rather high. That's because some academic studies have suggested that high accruals ratios tend to lead to lower profit or less profit growth.

Over the twelve months to September 2026, Nila Spaces recorded an accrual ratio of 0.88. As a general rule, that bodes poorly for future profitability. To wit, the company did not generate one whit of free cashflow in that time. Even though it reported a profit of ₹315.9m, a look at free cash flow indicates it actually burnt through ₹2.8b in the last year. Coming off the back of negative free cash flow last year, we imagine some shareholders might wonder if its cash burn of ₹2.8b, this year, indicates high risk.

Note: we always recommend investors check balance sheet strength. Click here to be taken to our balance sheet analysis of Nila Spaces.

Our Take On Nila Spaces' Profit Performance

As we have made quite clear, we're a bit worried that Nila Spaces didn't back up the last year's profit with free cashflow. For this reason, we think that Nila Spaces' statutory profits may be a bad guide to its underlying earnings power, and might give investors an overly positive impression of the company. But at least holders can take some solace from the 58% EPS growth in the last year. Of course, we've only just scratched the surface when it comes to analysing its earnings; one could also consider margins, forecast growth, and return on investment, among other factors.
